subject: PayFlux latency spike — leadership standby & customer update
messages:
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@payflux.com>
To: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@payflux.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden latency/errors (please advise)

David —

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx errors and tail latency for our darkest traffic at ~07:45 PST. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to 3.5% and p99 latency jumped from 420ms to ~2.6s. This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of EU users routed through your US region.

Attached is the compressed sample of 500 failing requests (payflux_error_sample.log) and a short CSV with payload sizes (payload-summary.csv). Our SREs can join a call immediately. We need an ETA for mitigation and any recommended temporary config changes (route, model variant, batching).

Alicia
Director, Platform Reliability
PayFlux

Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency/errors (please advise)

Thanks Alicia — and sorry for the disruption. We’re standing up a focused response now. Short plan:

- Immediate: open a 30-min triage call (joining link in thread).
- Short-term mitigation: we’ll evaluate fallback to a slightly lower-capacity model variant and temporarily tighten batching windows for affected routes.
- Investigations: telemetry + kernel-selection traces and GPU utilization across the pool.

Monica, Marcus — can you take lead on the telemetry and routing changes? Lauren / Sean, I’ll need leadership-level comms and a concise readout for PayFlux execs.

I’ve pulled the attached logs into an incident workspace: https://dashboard.redwood.example.com/teams/payflux/telemetry?range=6h

-David

Subject: Re: sudden latency/errors (please advise)

On it — quick notes from the infra side:

- Telemetry shows a correlated spike in kernel queue depth on GPU-14 and a short-lived thrash on KV cache evictions around 07:42 PST.
- One replica serving the EU route hit a memory pressure condition and the autoscaler added two pods; the traffic burst coincided with the scale-up window.
- Immediate mitigations I recommend: 1) pin PayFlux routes to replicas on the lower-utilization pool (policy id: payflux-isolate-02) and 2) roll back to model variant rdx-small-v2 for 10 minutes while we stabilize.

I’ll push a routing policy change and monitor. If successful we should see error rate drop in ~2–3 minutes post-change.

Attachment: incident-run-brief.txt (pushed to the incident drive).

—Marcus
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — joining the triage now. For the leadership touchpoint I recommend we:

1) Provide a one-page readout to PayFlux execs: impact summary (users affected, ingress boundaries), short-term actions taken, ETA for measurable improvement, and next steps.
2) Offer a credit estimate if the degradation persists >2 hours. Finance informed me of the current usage bands.
3) Keep updates at 30-minute cadence until p99 < 600ms and error rate < 0.5%.

I’ll draft the one-page and circulate for sign-off. Monica, can you grab the per-route traffic counts and customer-facing messaging language?

Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 18:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: PayFlux latency spike — leadership standby & customer update

Alicia —

Summary update (first 10 hours):
- Impact: ~3.2k checkout attempts were delayed; observable error rate peaked at 3.5% and has fallen to 0.45% after routing and variant rollback. Affected traffic window: 07:42–10:20 PST.
- Actions taken: isolated PayFlux routes to payflux-isolate-02 pool, rolled traffic to rdx-small-v2 for 22 minutes, tightened batching for high-payload requests, and applied a temporary KV cache size increase on replicas.
- Current status: p50=96ms, p95=280ms, p99=512ms; error rate steady at 0.45% and trending down.
- Next steps: 1) continue monitoring for 24 hours, 2) schedule a post-mortem with detailed kernel traces, 3) implement a permanent route affinity for PayFlux (planned rollout this week).

I’ve attached a one-page customer note (customer_status_note_v1.docx) for your review — Lauren, please sign off and I’ll send the external update.

We will also prepare an internal RCA draft and share the initial timeline for permanent mitigations by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
